summary: Assess social protection programmes against international standards and build an evidence-based action roadmap. Explore the course outline.
lede: International social protection standards provide reference points for policy analysts, programme evaluators and social security administrators reviewing benefit programmes. The training develops skills in mapping benefit provisions against standards, assessing coverage and adequacy evidence, and documenting governance and service-quality findings in an implementation roadmap. Exercises use sample programme information and Excel-based evidence tables; legal interpretation and actuarial modelling receive overview-level treatment.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who review social security provisions, oversee benefit administration or translate policy commitments into operational evidence. It suits staff who already work with social protection programmes and need a structured way to compare practice with international standards.
prerequisites: Prior experience with social protection policy, programme administration, evaluation or monitoring is recommended. You should be comfortable reviewing programme documents and working with basic tables; no coding or actuarial modelling is required.
